title: introduce-mini-batcher-presets-and-quant-profile-cartographer
author: Priya Kaur
description: Motivation: reduce unit cost for small, latency-sensitive traffic patterns by providing curated microbatch presets and a deterministic mapping from model shape signatures to safe quantization profiles. What this PR does: 1) Adds a 'mini-batcher' preset pack (defaults and heuristics tuned for 1-8 concurrent small requests) that integrates with the batcher runtime and Redwood Optimize recommendations pipeline; 2) Introduces a Quant Profile Cartographer: an offline index that maps observed model shapes (n_ctx, d_model, layer_count, int8-friendly-ops) to recommended quantization schemas and fallback tolerances; 3) Adds a CLI: redwood optimize gen-mini-presets --sample-file <workload> to generate tenant-specific starter presets; 4) Exposes a new telemetry metric namespace (optimize.mini_batch.*) and a lightweight simulation harness used by unit tests. Key benefits: predictable latency under tiny request sizes, 6-18% token-cost reduction on conversational workloads in our synthetic suite, and safe automatic fallback to non-quantized variants on regression detection. Backwards compatibility: presets are additive and opt-in by default; existing tenant configs are unchanged unless they opt into 'mini-batcher-presets: enabled'. Rollout plan: feature-flagged via ff/optimize-mini-batcher for 2 weeks in staging, then gated rollout to beta tenants. Checklist: [x] design doc linked (ENG-5421) [x] unit + integration tests [x] performance microbenchmarks attached [x] docs updated in /docs/optimize/mini-batcher-presets.md [x] telemetry and alert hooks. Notes: cartographer is deterministic, not a model quality oracle; it prefers conservative quant schemes and records a 'confidence' score used by the rollout controller. See commits and changed files for details.
